# Separate Geometry

Splits into the selected part and the rest, so each can be edited differently and joined back.

`lfs.separate_geometry` · Geometry

## How to use

Connect a Selection, then edit the two outputs separately.\
Use Join Geometry to bring the branches back together.\
Soft selection weights become a yes/no split at 0.5.

## Inputs

| Name | Identifier | Type | Default | Range / choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Geometry | `Geometry` | lfs.geometry | — | — | Geometry you want to edit. Connect a source; an unconnected input supplies no geometry. |
| Selection | `Selection` | lfs.float | 1 | min 0; max 1; step 0.01; accepts per-element values | What goes to Selection: weights of 0.5 or more. Lower weights go to Inverted; unconnected selects everything. |

## Outputs

| Name | Identifier | Type | Default | Range / choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Selection | `Selection` | lfs.geometry | — | — | Geometry whose selection weight is at least 0.5. Edit this branch separately. |
| Inverted | `Inverted` | lfs.geometry | — | — | Geometry whose selection weight is below 0.5. This is the part left outside your selection. |
